children: is taking preorders for a new range of laptops designed to bring its Android ecosystem and artificial-intelligence tools more closely together, as the company targets users who move between smartphones and computers.
The five Googlebook models, made by Acer, Asus, Dell, HP, and Lenovo, start at $899 and go up to $1,299. The first devices are scheduled to go on sale in the U.S. on October 4.

said the laptops are aimed initially at Android users rather than as a replacement for every type of computer. Android executive Sameer Samat described the launch as the first step in a longer-term effort in an interview with Axios.
The devices combine a desktop environment derived from ChromeOS with Android software, allowing users to run Android applications alongside Chrome, web apps, and Linux tools.
A key feature is Magic Pointer, which lets users call on Google's

Gemini AI by moving the cursor over content on the screen. Gemini can use the surrounding text, images, and other context to help with tasks such as scheduling events, reviewing email, and analyzing images.
The laptops can use traditional x86 processors or ARM-based chips, initially from Qualcomm
said Googlebook will coexist with Chromebooks, which remain important in education and business settings. The company has not said whether it will eventually launch a Pixel-branded version.
Shares were trading around 2% higher on Monday.

title: Googlebook laptops debut with Android integration, Gemini AI
